Name what they did well and state what next rubric level requires. Do not change marks. Do not comment on document-conversion artefacts. Do not make up explanations for reasoning given by marking agent that is unclear or incomplete.

We need craft feedback per criterion C1-C5. Use evidence from marking. Mention strengths and next level requirements. For C1: Very good 8/10. Strengths: identifies several ethical issues, links to engineering design, organisational context, stakeholders. Next level (Excellent) requires deeper stakeholder analysis, especially chip contract company interests/risks not analysed (technical issue). Also "stakeholder analysis is listed rather than deeply developed". So feedback: You identify several ethical issues and link them to engineering design and organisational context, and list stakeholders in INTRODUCTION. To reach Excellent, deepen stakeholder analysis—e.g., analyse the chip contract company’s interests and risks, not just list it. Also demonstrate understanding of BOTH context and stakeholder interest more fully.

C2: Very good 8/10. Strengths: for-and-against arguments with reasonable depth, clear decision. Next level: conclusions focus mainly on Rachel and her company; need decision guidance for several different stakeholders. Also technical issues: speculative claims about competitor shipping and Rachel losing job unsupported; no quantitative risk assessment; trade-off about large-scale testing not discussed. But for C2 specifically: "Conclusions focus mainly on Rachel and her company rather than decision guidance for several stakeholders." So feedback: Your for-and-against discussion in "DICUSSION: To Ship or Not to Ship" is balanced and reaches a clear decision. To reach Excellent, extend conclusions to give decision-making recommendations for several stakeholders (e.g., health department, chip supplier), and avoid unsupported speculation (competitor would ship, Rachel would lose job). Also consider quantitative risk to distinguish physical harm vs data loss.

C3: Very good 8/10. Strengths: logical structure supports clear conclusion, arguments generally compelling. Next level: systematic understanding of all stakeholders, especially chip supplier and health department. Also technical issue: NHS case called "almost identical" without evidence; EACE clause misapplied; "cannot be understated" phrase. But C3 focus: systematic understanding of ethical issues for all stakeholders. Feedback: Your report structure logically supports your "Not to Ship" conclusion, and arguments are compelling. To reach Excellent, demonstrate systematic understanding of ethical issues for all stakeholders—especially the chip supplier and health department—and ensure each stakeholder’s position is analysed, not just listed. Also strengthen evidence for comparisons (e.g., NHS case) and check ethical clause application.

C4: Very good 8/10. Strengths: relevant references and external case studies with qualitative evidence. Next level: quantitative evidence and substantiate every argument. Technical issues: no quantitative risk assessment; reference list incomplete/inconsistent; speculative claims unsupported; NHS case equivalence unsupported. Feedback: You use relevant references and external case studies (NHS, Volkswagen) with qualitative evidence. To reach Excellent, add quantitative evidence (e.g., failure likelihood, severity, test coverage) and substantiate every argument. Also fix reference list: BBC [3] lacks URL, [1] URL malformed, [4] author formatting unclear. Avoid unsupported claims (competitor shipping, job loss) and evidence the NHS case equivalence.

C5: Good 6/10. Strengths: required sections, fluent prose, relevant references. Next level: several types of visual elements competently, no incorrect language, relevant references extensively. Technical issues: no figures/tables; grammar errors; reference formatting; phrase "cannot be understated" wrong. Feedback: Your report has required sections and fluent prose. To reach Very good/Excellent, include several types of visual elements (e.g., decision flowchart, stakeholder map, risk table) and eliminate language errors: "cannot be understated" should be "cannot be overstated"; fix "The economic benefits of could very well" and "have her company might go under". Also complete and standardise references (BBC [3] URL, [1] URL, [4] author).
